title: Casimir-Electrostatic NEMS Pull-In: Bifurcation, Phase Diagrams & Physics-Informed Neural Networks
description:
Reproducible computational archive accompanying the article "Pull-in from rest under electrostatic and Casimir forces: Exact bounds, merger with the static fold at finite damping, and collapse asymptotics" (submitted to Physical Review E, 2026).

The code models the pull-in instability of a parallel-plate nano-electromechanical (NEMS) oscillator driven by both an electrostatic force and the attractive Casimir force. It (i) derives the closed-form saddle-node (fold) bifurcation separating the stable and pull-in regimes in the (electrostatic, Casimir) control plane, (ii) maps the dynamic pull-in threshold for release from rest by deterministic integration, including the numerical checks behind the rigorous bounds on that threshold, (iii) trains physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that solve the governing ODE, including a pull-in-safe rapidity parametrization for the movable pole and a parametric PINN that learns the fold boundary purely from the force-balance residual, (iv) computes the finite-temperature Lifshitz correction and the resulting thermal shift of the pull-in voltage, and (v) estimates the squeeze-film damping regimes of representative gold actuators (new in 1.2.0). All results, models, logs and the publication figures regenerate deterministically from a single fixed seed (42), CPU-only, in float64. See README.md and SEEDS.md.
